findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving the service user near-administrative control over compute, storage and serverless resources. Compromise of this user's credentials would allow data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and takeover of any EC2/Lambda resource.

A long-lived IAM access key is created for a highly privileged user instead of using temporary credentials via an IAM role; the secret is stored in Terraform state in plaintext because no PGP key is supplied, exposing it to anyone with state access.

No pgp_key is configured, so the access key secret is written unencrypted to Terraform state (and the encrypted_secret attribute referenced in the output will be empty/null), meaning the credential is only protected by state file storage controls.
The svc_deploy_key_material output exposes access key material without marking it sensitive = true, so it is printed to console logs and CI output where it can be harvested.
A highly privileged long-lived IAM user is created with no MFA enforcement and no permissions boundary, relying solely on static access keys for authentication.
